column1: # Checker qualification. Does a check fail when the thing it protects is broken?
# checker <TAB> command <TAB> control <TAB> expect <TAB> mutation [<TAB> premise]
# The command is the checker, run in a throwaway worktree of HEAD after the
# mutation has been applied to it. `expect` is what a checker worth having must
# say.
# The premise is optional and is run first, in the same worktree. Exit 1 means
# the control cannot be staged in this checkout — reported as not applying,
# never as held and never as met. Any other failure is unrunnable, so a premise
# that errors is loud. A checker whose every fail-expecting control is not
# applying is named as never shown failing here and refuses the gate (#233),
# so a checker whose teeth all need a premise also needs one control that
# stages its own.
# The six controls come from v3.2 conformance amendments 2.1. The first four
# all move the marker and the property together, so a checker keyed on a
# lexical shadow tracks every one of them; decoupled_violation and
# decoupled_satisfaction are the two that pull them apart, and the amendments
# record that decoupled_violation alone caught four cheats out of four.
# AUTHORSHIP. Amendments 2.2 requires the mutations be written by something
# that has not seen the checker, because whoever writes both writes mutations
# its own checker survives. These were authored by a subagent given the
# obligation in prose and forbidden the checker's source; the session that
# built the runner did not write them and did not read secret-scan first. That
# is as close as this gets, and it is unverifiable from inside — a report that
# it was blind is worth nothing on its own — so this records the method rather
# than claiming the property.
# The values are assembled by the mutation rather than written out here, and
# that is not cosmetic. A table of mutations for a CREDENTIAL checker is itself
# full of credential-shaped strings, and the first version of this file was
# caught by the very scanner it qualifies — correctly. The credential belongs
# in the worktree the checker is pointed at, never in the diff that adds the
# table. Keeping the two apart is the same distinction the checker exists to
# draw, applied to its own fixture.
secret

column1: # memory: invariant 6 as a command, bin/memory-scan. Twelve controls, six per
# half of the property, authored blind (amendments §2.2) by an agent given the

# Where a lexical checker for this property is probably blind: it will look for the path `projects/<name>/memory/` in `git ls-files`, so a canonical memory file (lessons.md, ledger.tsv, DEVLOG.md ...) tracked one level up or under docs/ is invisible to it, while a directory merely *named* memory anywhere else trips it (the tree already tracks engine/harness/lib/memory.sh and templates/commission/, so a bare-token grep would fail a clean tree). For maintenance.log it will read the root .gitignore for the literal token, so it is blind to a nested .gitignore (projects/.gitignore with `*.log` overrides the root negation), to rule order (the last matching line wins, so an unnegated line followed by its negation ignores nothing), and it will mistake a comment or a `maintenance.log.*` pattern for a rule. git's own `check-ignore --no-index` is the only honest oracle, and plain `check-ignore` is itself blind for a file that is already tracked, which both existing maintenance.logs are.

column1: # decoupled_violation: the branch writes a pending section and commits it, then folds that section itself, by hand and without a flaw: the current section archived verbatim with its trailing blank line dropped, its row put directly above the newest 0<letters> row with the heading's own title, the pending section made current under the next id, the marker moved on to the id after that, the pending file deleted. Every marker, heading, row and file agrees, and the last commit on its own looks exactly like a fold. But main never held that pending file. Against the merge-base the current id moved while no pending file main holds was removed, which is a section written in by hand. A checker keyed on the tree's shape, or comparing with HEAD~1 or the branch's own commits rather than the merge-base, passes it. Written from the property in prose.

column1: # decoupled_satisfaction: the current section amended in place, under its own id: a paragraph added just above its closing `---` that names the next id in prose. It shares no syntax with the obvious legitimate change (a new file under pending/). It changes the one section a hand-written handoff would change, and it mentions the id a hand-written section would take, but the id, heading, marker, rows and archives are all as they were, and editing the current section's body in place is allowed. A checker that compares the current section's bytes with the merge-base's, or that treats any mention of the next id as a section written in, refuses it. Written from the property in prose.
